hints: Focus on the structure of the target, 2-chloro-2-methylpropane is $(CH_3)_3CCl$, a tertiary chloroalkane, so think which reactions put Cl on that tertiary carbon.
Check set 1 first, addition of $HCl$ to the alkene $CH_2C(CH_3)CH_3$ follows Markovnikov's rule with $Cl$ adding to the more stable tertiary carbocation.
Now link the other two routes, $OH$ to $Cl$ substitution with $SOCl_2$ and free radical chlorination of the alkane, and ask if either can also place Cl at the tertiary position.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target molecule**

Great start, let's draw what we want. 2-chloro-2-methylpropane is $(CH_3)_3CCl$.

It is also called tert-butyl chloride:
$$ (CH_3)_3CCl $$
The Cl is on a tertiary carbon, bonded to three other carbons.

**Test set 1 - electrophilic addition**

Reagents are $CH_2C(CH_3)CH_3$ (2-methylpropene) + $HCl(g)$.

This is electrophilic addition across the $C=C$ bond. By Markovnikov's rule, $H^+$ adds to the $CH_2$ end to give the stable tertiary carbocation, then $Cl^-$ adds to the tertiary carbon:
$$ CH_2=C(CH_3)_2 + HCl \rightarrow (CH_3)_3CCl $$
So set 1 works perfectly.

**Test set 2 - nucleophilic substitution**

Reagents are $CH_3C(CH_3)(OH)CH_3$ (2-methylpropan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol) + $SOCl_2$.

$SOCl_2$ is a classic chlorinating agent that replaces the $-OH$ group by $-Cl$:
$$ (CH_3)_3COH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow (CH_3)_3CCl + SO_2 + HCl $$
So set 2 also gives the target.

**Test set 3 - free radical substitution**

Reagents are $CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_3$ (2-methylpropane) + $Cl_2$ with UV light.

This is free radical substitution of an alkane. The molecule has nine primary $C-H$ bonds and one tertiary $C-H$ bond. Replacement of the tertiary H gives $(CH_3)_3CCl$:
$$ (CH_3)_3CH + Cl_2 \xrightarrow{UV} (CH_3)_3CCl + HCl $$
Other isomers also form, but the question only asks for it as one of the products, so set 3 counts. All three work.

options.A: Correct and well done. Set 1 gives it by Markovnikov addition, set 2 gives it by $OH$ to $Cl$ substitution with $SOCl_2$, and set 3 gives it as one product (in fact the major product) of free radical chlorination at the tertiary position.
options.B: Close but incomplete. You correctly spotted sets 1 and 2, but dismissed set 3. Remember UV chlorination of 2-methylpropane replaces the single tertiary H much faster than primary H, so 2-chloro-2-methylpropane is formed alongside 1-chloro isomers.
options.C: Not quite. You correctly spotted sets 1 and 3, but missed set 2. Tertiary alcohols react readily with $SOCl_2$ at room temperature to replace $-OH$ with $-Cl$, giving exactly $(CH_3)_3CCl$.
options.D: Not quite. You correctly spotted sets 2 and 3, but missed set 1. Addition of $HCl$ to 2-methylpropene is the textbook Markovnikov route to tert-butyl chloride, with $Cl$ ending up on the tertiary carbon.
